claim: Barotrauma effects can start when fish are caught from deeper than about 30 feet.
title: Catching Fish from Deep Water - Barotrauma
publisher: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks
quote: Under 30 feet is generally considered safe, and over 30 feet is when barotrauma effects can start being present.

claim: The rapid pressure change as a fish is reeled up makes its swim bladder expand.

claim: Bass have no physical outlet to vent gas from the gas (swim) bladder.
title: Catching Fish from Deep Water - Barotrauma
publisher: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks
quote: Many fish species, such as walleye, bass, and sunfish, do not have a physical outlet to the gas bladder

claim: In bass the gas leaves slowly, diffusing into the blood and out through the gills.

publisher: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks
quote: pressure is regulated by gas diffusing through the bladder and into the blood stream through a valve, and eventually being released through the gills

claim: Signs of barotrauma include bulging eyes, a swollen belly and the fish floating upside down or on its side.
title: Deep trouble: Protecting your catch from barotrauma
quote: Bulging eyes, a swollen belly, fish floating upside down or on its side, and even internal organs protruding through the throat

claim: Fish that cannot submerge risk being struck by boats and eaten by birds.

publisher: North Dakota Game and Fish Department
quote: being struck by boats or increased predation as they become easy prey for birds like gulls or pelicans

claim: A descending device is a weight attached to the fish's lip that sinks it back to its original depth.

quote: a weight attached to the fish’s lip that sinks them to their original depth for release

claim: Returning the fish to depth recompresses the swim bladder.
title: Understanding Barotrauma

claim: Descending only treats the swim bladder and does not reverse other internal injuries.

claim: Avoid putting fish on hot surfaces like engine covers.
title: Catch and Release Guidelines: To Reduce Mortality in Black Basses and Other Fishes
quote: No hot surfaces like engine covers or sun-drenched boat decks.

claim: Carpeted decks can be abrasive to fish, even when wet.

quote: Carpeted decks may be abrasive, even when wet.

claim: Hold black bass by the lower jaw without hyper-extending it.

claim: Keep a fish out of water no longer than you can hold your breath.
